steps.scene: You're in the left-hand lane. A red X lights up on the gantry above your lane. The lanes to your right show a 50 mph limit.

options.text: Carry on — it warns that the lane closes further ahead
Stop under the gantry and wait
Move into an open lane when it's safe, before the gantry

question.explanation: The red X closes your lane from that gantry. The other lanes are still open, so move over and keep to their limit.

steps.title: Red X: the lane is closed
steps.body: A red X above a lane means you MUST NOT drive past it in that lane. It isn't advice — there may be a crash, a breakdown or people ahead.

question.prompt: What does a red X above a motorway lane mean?

options.text: You must not drive in that lane beyond the sign
Slow down — the lane may close later on
The lane is kept for emergency vehicles, but you may use it

question.explanation: Red X signals are enforced by cameras. Driving under one puts you in the path of whatever closed the lane.

steps.scene: Every lane on the gantry ahead suddenly shows a red X, with red lamps flashing.

options.text: Leave at the next exit
Stop and wait — don't change lanes or drive on
Carry on slowly along the hard shoulder

question.explanation: A red X over every lane closes the whole carriageway at that point. Stop and wait for the signals to change.

a.label: Red X over hard shoulder
a.body: It's shut as a running lane. Use it only for an emergency or a breakdown.

b.label: Speed limit over hard shoulder
b.body: It's open as a running lane. Keep to the limit and look out for broken-down vehicles.

question.prompt: A speed limit is shown above the hard shoulder. What does it mean?

options.text: You may stop there if you need a rest
You may drive in it as a normal lane
Keep out of it — it's for emergencies only

question.explanation: On some motorways the hard shoulder opens as a lane at busy times. The signal above it tells you which it is right now.

steps.title: Limits that change
steps.body: A speed limit in a red ring on a gantry is mandatory. It changes with the traffic to keep everyone moving steadily and cut stop-start bunching.

question.prompt: Why do some motorways use variable speed limits?

options.text: To suggest a comfortable speed — they're only advice
To reduce bunching and keep traffic flowing
To let traffic go faster when roads are quiet

question.explanation: A steady 50 mph moves more traffic than racing to 70 and braking to a stop. Cameras often enforce the limit.

steps.scene: You're in the right-hand lane. The gantry ahead shows an arrow pointing left and a 50 limit. The road beyond looks completely clear.

options.text: Move left in good time and slow to 50 mph
Carry on until you can see what the problem is
Use the hard shoulder to get past the hazard

question.explanation: Gantry signs warn of queues and hazards you can't see yet. Obey them even when the road looks clear.

steps.wrongBelief: A red X is just an early warning that the lane closes somewhere ahead.

question.prompt: A red X shows above your lane, but the cars ahead in it keep going. What should you do?

options.text: Follow them — if they're carrying on, the lane can't be closed yet
Move to an open lane — you must not pass the red X in this one
Put your hazard lights on and stay in the lane

question.explanation: Other drivers breaking the rule doesn't make it safe. The lane is closed from the gantry, whatever they do.

steps.repairNote: The lane is closed now, not later. You must not drive past a red X in that lane.
